description: 32x24 RGB/8; a base layer with a clipped layer above it (clipping flag set).

expectationSource.method: psd-tools PSDImage.open() for structure and layer records; composite() for compositePixels; layer.numpy() for layerPixels. No Agogo code in the loop.
manualChecks: compositePixels is deliberately NOT asserted for this fixture. The sidecar's composite samples come from psd-tools re-rendering the layer stack, and Agogo renders it too; those are two different renderers. Where the stack is plain source-over they agree (every other fixture asserts compositePixels and passes), but this fixture exists precisely to exercise semantics where two renderers are not obliged to agree pixel-for-pixel. Per-layer rasters are still asserted via layerPixels, which is unambiguous. Comparing renderers here would assert that Agogo matches psd-tools' arithmetic, which is not the contract. Clipping-group compositing differs between implementations.

writer.lossyReason: PLAN.md S.10.3: SavePSD hard-clips a clipped layer's stored bounds to the intersection with its clip base - (8,6) 18x14 is re-exported as (8,9) 11x11 - so pixels outside the base are destroyed on save. Photoshop keeps them; moving the base there brings the hidden content back. Verified by reading both the fixture and _dump/rgb8-clipping.reexport.psd with psd-tools. PLAN.md S.10.2: psdexport emits layer channels in its own fixed order (0,1,2,-1; gray 0,-1) and always emits an alpha channel, because the engine model is RGBA. This fixture was authored with alpha first (-1,0,1,2) or with no alpha channel at all, so every re-exported record's channelIds differ in order and the flattened records gain a -1. The PSD spec does not prescribe channel order and readers key on the ID, so this is a spelling difference rather than lost data: the set of IDs is otherwise unchanged, the -2 user mask channel included. psd-tools 1.19.0 and ImageMagick 6.9.12-98 both read the re-export correctly. psdRecords[2].bounds is the record-level face of layers[2].bounds, already listed here; it needs its own entry because the record leg reads bounds from the raw layer record rather than from the reconstructed model.

externalVerification.notes: tools/psdfixtures/verify_dump.py --identify re-read the Agogo re-export with psd-tools 1.19.0 and ImageMagick 6.9.12-98; both accepted the file and reported the expected structure. Field-level losses are listed in writer.lossy with writer.lossyReason. See testdata/VERIFICATION.md.
